newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB expects 96/97 2nd half to match yr ago.
newsitem.headline: NAB expects 96/97 2nd half to match yr ago.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) managing director Don Argus said on Thursday he thought the bank's second half profit for the 1996/97 year to September 30 could match the result in the same period a year earlier.
"We would like to think we could," Argus told reporters when asked if the bank's second half year result could match its performance in the corresponding period of 1995/96.
Argus said the impact of lower interest rates would start to be felt in the second half, but he hoped to absorb this, depending on economic conditions.
"There will be an impact. There wouldn't be any doubt about that," Argus said.
National Australia Bank (NAB), the nation's largest bank, earlier reported a 14.1 percent rise in net profit to A$1.14 billion for the six months ended March 31, 1997.
In the year to September 30, 1996, NAB reported a net profit of A$2.10 billion, after an abnormal gain of A$3 million.
Analysts expect NAB to post a net profit before abnormals of between A$2.23 and A$2.47 billion for the 1996/97 year.
